title: Cueca (handkerchief dance)
summary: The cueca is a couple dance of Chile, Bolivia and Argentina: two dancers circle one another, waving handkerchiefs in a playful courtship, to guitar, hand claps and drum that sway between 6/8 and 3/4.
howToPlay: Five lanes stand for the left step, the right step, the stamp, the floor brush and the hand claps.
Beats arrive at the line; strike the matching lane as each one lands.
Count in groups of six pulses: the walk leans in two groups of three, and the other song turns them into three groups of two.
Play the walking song first, then the six-against-three song and the brushing song.
rules: Each bar has six pulses; in 6/8 the accents fall on pulse one and four, in 3/4 on one, three and five.
Songs repeat twice; a stroke on the pulse is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The tempo is taught slower than the dance is usually performed.
heritageNote: The cueca is danced at family gatherings, festivals and national celebrations in Chile, Bolivia and Argentina, each region with its own steps and tempo. Chile named it a national dance in 1979, and Bolivia recognised its cueca as national heritage in 2015.
credits: Tradition: cueca of Chile, Bolivia and Argentina; step patterns written for this game
